title: Add `find_objects()` function
description:
Adds a function to find objects in code:

``` r
library(gradecode)
library(dplyr)
.user_code <- "band_members %>% full_join(band_instruments)"

find_objects(.user_code)
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> band_members %>% full_join(band_instruments)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> objects
#> Found 2 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> band_members %>% full_join(band_instruments)
#> ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> band_members %>% full_join(band_instruments)
#>                            ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
```

If `match` is specified, `find_objects()` only finds that object
```r
find_objects(.user_code, match = band_members)
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> band_members %>% full_join(band_instruments)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> object band_members
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> band_members %>% full_join(band_instruments)
#> ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
```

If `match` does not exist in the code, `find_objects()` returns nothing
```r
find_objects(.user_code, match = storms)
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> band_members %>% full_join(band_instruments)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> object storms
#> Found 0 results.
```

`match = dplyr::band_members` can find the object `band_members`
```r
find_objects(.user_code, match = dplyr::band_members)
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> band_members %>% full_join(band_instruments)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> object dplyr::band_members
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> band_members %>% full_join(band_instruments)
#> ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
```

But `match = "dplyr::band_members"` looks for an exact name, so it can't find the object `band_members`
```r
find_objects(.user_code, match = "dplyr::band_members")
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> band_members %>% full_join(band_instruments)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> object "dplyr::band_members"
#> Found 0 results.
```

`uses_function()` returns `TRUE` if `match` appears in the code
```r
uses_object(.user_code, match = band_members)
#> [1] TRUE
uses_object(.user_code, match = band_instruments)
#> [1] TRUE
uses_object(.user_code, match = storms)
#> [1] FALSE

uses_object(.user_code, match = dplyr::band_members)
#> [1] TRUE
uses_object(.user_code, match = "dplyr::band_members")
#> [1] FALSE
```

title: Add `find_parent()`
description:
Add function `find_parent()` to find the parent node(s) of the results of a `find_*()` function.

This PR also introduces a new system for adding examples to documentation. Examples are stored in the `man/examples` directory, to make it easier to run them interactively. An internal helper function, `use_example()`, is added to make it easier to work with the examples directory.

Closes #51.

## Usage

``` r
library(gradecode)

.user_code <- "mtcars %>%
  mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
  summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))"
```

The parent of an argument is the call containing the argument

```r
.user_code %>%
  find_arguments(arg(na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  find_parent()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mtcars %>%
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> argument na.rm = TRUE > parents
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mtcars %>%
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
#>                      ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
```

The parent of a function is the call containing the function and its arguments

```r
.user_code %>%
  find_functions(mean) %>%
  find_parent()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mtcars %>%
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> function mean > parents
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mtcars %>%
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
#>                      ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾

.user_code %>%
  find_functions("summarize") %>%
  find_parent()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mtcars %>%
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> function "summarize" > parents
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mtcars %>%
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
#>   ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
```

The parent of an operator is the left- and right-hand side of the operator

```r
.user_code %>%
  find_operators("*") %>%
  find_parent()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mtcars %>%
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> operator "*" > parents
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mtcars %>%
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#>               ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾           
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
```

But remember that, based on order of operations, an operator's parent may contain more than you expect

```r
.user_code %>%
  find_operators("/") %>%
  find_parent()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mtcars %>%
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> operator "/" > parents
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mtcars %>%
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#>               ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾     
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
```

The same applies to pipes

```r
.user_code %>%
  find_pipes() %>%
  find_parent()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mtcars %>%
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> pipes > parents
#> Found 2 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mtcars %>%
#> ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#> ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾    
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> mtcars %>%
#> ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
#>   mutate(kg = wt * 1000 / 2.2) %>%
#> ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
#>   summarize(avg_kg = mean(kg, na.rm = TRUE))
#> ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
```

title: Give XML results new S3 classes
description: `gradecode` results are now classed as `gradecode_xml_node`, `gradecode_xml_nodeset`, or `gradecode_xml_list`. These classes also come with new print methods to make it easier to inspect `gradecode` objects' XML results. ## Examples Set `options(gradecode.print_xml_all_attrs = TRUE)` to suppress attributes of all but outer nodes, cleaning up the output. `find_arguments()` can produce nested results.

title: Add function for finding the values of arguments
description:
Adds `find_argument_values()`.
Closes #50.

## Usage

`find_argument_values()` can be called after `find_arguments()`:

``` r
library(gradecode)

.user_code <- "mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)"

.user_code %>% 
  find_arguments("na.rm") %>% 
  find_argument_values()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> argument "na.rm" > argument values
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                                             ‾‾‾‾
```

after `find_functions()`:

```r
.user_code %>% 
  find_functions(mean) %>% 
  find_argument_values()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> function mean > argument values
#> Found 2 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>      ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                                             ‾‾‾‾
```

or on its own:

```r
find_argument_values(.user_code)
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> argument values
#> Found 5 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>      ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                                             ‾‾‾‾
#> 
#> ── Result 3 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>            ‾‾
#> 
#> ── Result 4 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                       ‾
#> 
#> ── Result 5 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                               ‾‾‾
```

title: Add `as.list()` method for `gradecode_found` objects
description:
``` r
library(gradecode)

gradecode_found <- find_functions("mean(1:10, na.rm = TRUE)", mean) %>%
  find_arguments() %>%
  find_operators(":")

as.list(gradecode_found) %>% str()
#> List of 3
#>  $ :List of 3
#>   ..$ type   : chr "function"
#>   ..$ request: chr "mean"
#>   ..$ result : chr "mean"
#>  $ :List of 3
#>   ..$ type   : chr "argument"
#>   ..$ request: chr NA
#>   ..$ result : chr [1:2] "1:10" "na.rm = TRUE"
#>  $ :List of 3
#>   ..$ type   : chr "operator"
#>   ..$ request: chr "\":\""
#>   ..$ result : chr ":"
```

Use the `as_xml` argument to get `$result` as XML instead of text.

```r
as.list(gradecode_found, as_xml = TRUE)
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$type
#> [1] "function"
#> 
#> [[1]]$request
#> [1] "mean"
#> 
#> [[1]]$result
#> {xml_nodeset (1)}
#> [1] <expr line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="4" start="26" end="29">\n  <SYMB ...

#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]]$type
```

title: Allow searching for arguments by name (regardless of value)
description:
If the `match` argument of `find_arguments()` is a character vector, find arguments by name regardless of value.

``` r
library(gradecode)
.user_code <- "mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)"

find_arguments(.user_code, match = "na.rm")
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> argument na.rm
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                                     ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
```

If `match` is a character vector of length > 1, find any of those arguments.

```r
find_arguments(.user_code, match = c("mean", "sd"))
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> argument mean > NA sd
#> Found 2 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                          ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
```

Closes #45.

title: Avoid multiple warnings about unknown RStudio themes
description:
Suppresses `cli`'s warning about unknown RStudio themes after the first opportunity to trigger the warning, to avoid it being displayed multiple times.

As a bonus, `highlighted_user_code` is now stored inside the `gradecode_found` object. Previously, code highlighting was rerun for each individual result. Storing the highlighted code gives a significant speedup to printing `gradecode_found` objects with many results.

# Before
```r
find_arguments(c("rnorm(x)", "runif(y)"))
#>
#> ── gradecode found ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> rnorm(x)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> functions > arguments
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> rnorm(x)
#> 
#> Warning messages:
#>   1: In code_theme_default_rstudio() :
#>   cli does not know this RStudio theme: 'Flat White {rsthemes}'.
#> Set `options(cli.ignore_unknown_rstudio_theme = TRUE)` to suppress this warning
#> 2: In code_theme_default_rstudio() :
#>   cli does not know this RStudio theme: 'Flat White {rsthemes}'.
#> Set `options(cli.ignore_unknown_rstudio_theme = TRUE)` to suppress this warning
#> 3: In code_theme_default_rstudio() :
#>   cli does not know this RStudio theme: 'Flat White {rsthemes}'.
#> Set `options(cli.ignore_unknown_rstudio_theme = TRUE)` to suppress this warning
```

# After
```r
find_arguments("rnorm(x)")
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> rnorm(x)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> functions > arguments
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> rnorm(x)
#> 
#> Warning message:
#>   In code_theme_default_rstudio() :
#>   cli does not know this RStudio theme: 'Flat White {rsthemes}'.
#> Set `options(cli.ignore_unknown_rstudio_theme = TRUE)` to suppress this warning
```

Closes #43.

title: Fix duplication of output in multi-line user code
description:
Reverts "Reimplement `inbetween()` for better performance (#39)" be2f23e

Unfortunately, the PR included an oversight that meant `inbetween()` would not generate `integer(0)` as expected for sequential numbers.
That meant that `emphasize_found()`, which adds underlining to the result of `find_*()` functions, did not correctly extract lines to apply formatting. For example, when looking for the lines between line 1 and 2, `emphasize_found()`should find nothing, but the bug in `inbetween()` meant if found lines 2 and 1 and reprinted them.

This PR also adds tests of `inbetween()` to ensure that this bug does not recur.

``` r
library(gradecode)

"rnorm(1)
runif(2)" %>% 
  find_functions()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> rnorm(1)
#> runif(2)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> functions
#> Found 2 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> rnorm(1)
#> ‾‾‾‾‾   
#> runif(2)
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> rnorm(1)
#> runif(2)
#> ‾‾‾‾‾

c("rnorm(1)", "runif(2)") %>% 
  find_functions()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> rnorm(1)
#> runif(2)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> functions
#> Found 2 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> rnorm(1)
#> ‾‾‾‾‾   
#> runif(2)
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> rnorm(1)
#> runif(2)
#> ‾‾‾‾‾

c("rnorm(1)", "runif(2)", "rpois(3)") %>% 
  find_functions()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> rnorm(1)
#> runif(2)
#> rpois(3)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> functions
#> Found 3 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> rnorm(1)
#> ‾‾‾‾‾   
#> runif(2)
#> rpois(3)
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> rnorm(1)
#> runif(2)
#> ‾‾‾‾‾   
#> rpois(3)
#> 
#> ── Result 3 ──
```

title: Reimplement `inbetween()` for better performance
description:
This won't make much of an impact, but sometimes it's just fun to see those `bench::mark()` numbers go down.

``` r
old_inbetween <- function(x, y) {
  x <- floor(x)
  y <- ceiling(y)
  setdiff(seq.int(x, y), c(x, y))
}

inbetween <- function(x, y) {
  # Find first integer greater than `x`
  x <- floor(x + 1)
  # Find first integer less than `y`
  y <- ceiling(y - 1)
  seq.int(x, y)
}

bench::mark(old = old_inbetween(47.1, 200.9), new = inbetween(47.1, 200.9))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   expression      min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec`
#>   <bch:expr> <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl>
#> 1 old         17.56µs  22.64µs    43033.    7.15KB     8.61
#> 2 new          1.34µs   1.53µs   517736.        0B    51.8
```

Adding `xml_find_all.list()` allows subsequent `find_*()` functions after a call to `find_arguments()`.

``` r
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> functions > arguments > functions

```

Closes #36.

title: Add `recurse` argument to `find_arguments()`
description:
Adds a `recurse` argument to `find_arguments()`.

When `recurse` is `TRUE`, `find_arguments()` finds arguments to all functions below the current node:

``` r
.user_code <- "mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)"

find_arguments(.user_code, recurse = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> arguments
#> Found 3 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#>      ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾               
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                 ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾ 
#> 
#> ── Result 3 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#>            ‾‾
```

When `recurse` is `FALSE`, `find_arguments()` only finds arguments to the top-level function:

```r
find_arguments(.user_code, recurse = FALSE)
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> arguments
#> Found 2 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#>      ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾               
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                 ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
```

The default value of `recurse` is `NULL`. This recurses if `find_arguments()` is not called directly after `find_functions`:

```r
find_arguments(.user_code)
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> arguments
#> Found 3 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#>      ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾               
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                 ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾ 
#> 
#> ── Result 3 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#>            ‾‾
```

If `find_arguments()` is called directly after `find_functions()`, it defaults to a non-recursive search which only finds arguments of the previously found function(s):

```r
find_functions(.user_code, mean) %>% find_arguments()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> function mean > arguments
#> Found 2 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#>      ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾               
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                 ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾
```

<sup>Created on 2022-09-02 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

Closes #34 and closes #35.

title: Compare character representations of XML in `find_arguments()`
description:
`all.equal()` fails to find differences when comparing XML nodes with different contents.
To fix this, we convert the nodes to their character representations before comparing.

``` r
.user_code <- "mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)"

find_arguments(.user_code, match = arg(na.rm = TRUE))
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> functions > argument na.rm = TRUE
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>                                     ‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾‾

find_arguments(.user_code, match = arg(10))
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> functions > argument 10
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mean(rnorm(10, mean = 1, sd = 0.1), na.rm = TRUE)
#>            ‾‾
```

<sup>Created on 2022-08-31 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

This problem could be solved using either `as.character()` or `xml2::as_list()`.
I opted for `as.character()` because it's faster:

``` r
x <- arg(na.rm = TRUE)[[1]]
y <- arg(na.rm = TRUE)[[1]]
z <- arg(sd = 0.1)[[1]]

bench::mark(
  as.character = isTRUE(all.equal(as.character(x), as.character(y))),
  as_list = isTRUE(all.equal(xml2::as_list(x), xml2::as_list(y)))
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   expression        min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec`
#>   <bch:expr>   <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl>
#> 1 as.character    159µs    166µs     5877.    93.9KB     17.5
#> 2 as_list         921µs    961µs     1018.    96.8KB     19.4

bench::mark(
  as.character = isTRUE(all.equal(as.character(x), as.character(z))),
  as_list = isTRUE(all.equal(xml2::as_list(x), xml2::as_list(z)))
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   expression        min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec`
#>   <bch:expr>   <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl>
#> 1 as.character    167µs 174.71µs     5563.        0B     17.0
#> 2 as_list         989µs   1.04ms      901.        0B     19.8
```

Closes #28.

title: `find_operators()` can now find all operators listed in `?Syntax`
description:
- `find_operators()` now looks for all operators listed in [`?Syntax`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/Syntax.html)'s order of operator precedence:

```
:: :::
$ @
[ [[
^
- +
:
%any% |>
* /
+ -
< > <= >= == !=
!
& &&
| ||
~
-> ->>
<- <<-
=
?
```

- If `match` is a vector, `find_operators()` now looks for _any_ of the matching operators.

Closes #25.

## Examples

### Supported operators

``` r
"a <- 1" %>% find_operators()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> a <- 1
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> operators
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> a <- 1
#>   ‾‾
"1 == 1" %>% find_operators()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 1 == 1
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> operators
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> 1 == 1
#>   ‾‾
"TRUE && FALSE" %>% find_operators()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> TRUE && FALSE
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> operators
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> TRUE && FALSE
#>      ‾‾
"mpg ~ wt" %>% find_operators()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mpg ~ wt
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> operators
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> mpg ~ wt
#>     ‾
"?help" %>% find_operators()
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ?help
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> operators
#> Found 1 result.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> ?help
#> ‾
```

<sup>Created on 2022-08-31 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

### Vector `match`

``` r
"a >= b || c != d" %>%
  find_operators(match = c("<", "<=", ">=", ">", "==", "!="))
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> a >= b || c != d
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> operator c("<", "<=", ">=", ">", "==", "!=")
#> Found 2 results.
#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──
#> a >= b || c != d
#>   ‾‾            
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
#> a >= b || c != d
#>             ‾‾
```

title: Store grades from `fail_if_not_found()` in `gradecode_found`
description:
- Adds a `$push_grade()` method and `grades` list to `gradecode_found` objects.
- `fail_if_not_found()` and `fail_if_not_found()` now add grades to the `gradecode_found` object if called outside `grade_this()`.

``` r
library(gradecode)
library(gradethis)

"mean(rnorm(10))" %>% 
  find_pipes() %>% 
  fail_if_not_found("I expected a pipe.") %>% 
  find_rhs() %>% 
  find_functions(mean) %>%
  fail_if_not_found("I expected `mean()` after the pipe.")
#> 
#> ── gradecode found ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> mean(rnorm(10))
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> pipes (✖) > rhs > function mean (✖)
#> Found 0 results.
#> 
#> ── Grades ──
#> ✖ I expected a pipe.
#> ✖ I expected `mean()` after the pipe.
```

If called within `grade_this()`, `fail_if_*_found()` still signals the grade condition as usual.

``` r
grade_this({
  .user_code %>% 
    find_pipes() %>% 
    fail_if_not_found("I expected a pipe.") %>% 
    find_rhs() %>% 
    find_functions(mean) %>%
    fail_if_not_found("I expected `mean()` after the pipe.")
})(mock_this_exercise(.user_code = "mean(rnorm(10))"))
#> <gradethis_graded: [Incorrect] I expected a pipe.>
```

``` r
#> 
#> ── Result 2 ──
```

``` r
uses_pipe("10 %>% rnorm() |> mean()", match = "%>%")

find_pipes("10 %>% rnorm() |> mean()", match = "%>%")

#> 10 %>% rnorm() |> mean()
#> 
#> ── Request ──
#> pipe `%>%`

#> 
#> ── Result 1 ──

uses_pipe("10 %>% rnorm() |> mean()", match = "|>")

find_pipes("10 %>% rnorm() |> mean()", match = "|>")

#>
```

1. supporting `gradecode_found()` objects that have `user_code` but no `requests`.

title: Ensure syntax highlighting does not use bold or underline
description:
Bold and underline styles are used to emphasize found code in `print.gradecde_found()`. If they are used for regular syntax highlighting, this could distract and confuse the user.

However, these styles (especially bold) are often used in `cli` code themes. To ensure they are not applied as syntax highlighting, we have to remove them in `get_code_styles()`.

Previously, `get_code_styles()` would only remove the strings "bold" and "underline". `get_code_styles()` now removes anything that evaluates to a bold or underline style after going through `cli::make_ansi_styles()`. This ensures themes that include precomputed styles will still not include bold or underline.

description:

title: Add `highlight_xml()`
description: Adds custom-built functionality for highlighting XML code with `print(as_xml = TRUE)`. The theme used for XML highlighting matches that used by `cli` for code highlighting. That means in RStudio, the highlighting can draw from your RStudio theme. ## Examples ### Tomorrow theme ### Dawn theme

title: Use `highlite` packge
description: Using [`highlite`](https://github.com/jimhester/highlite) rather than `cli::code_highlight()` allows highlighting to apply to both R code and XML nodes.

title: Emphasize substrings of the original `user_code` when printing `gradecode_found` results
description: Previously, the emphasized code was the result of applying `xml_text()` to the XML parse data. This lost all non-syntactic formatting (i.e. whitespace) which had to be re-added with `styler`. This process had the disadvantages that the code would not formatted the exact way the user wrote it, and that line breaks would be added inconsistently if more that one line of code needed to be emphasized. ## Before ## After
